text:
[CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/html/2010.14395) crops a randomly positioned contiguous subsequence of length floor(η·L): a fixed proportion conditional on history length, rather than a randomly sampled suffix length. Two augmented views support an auxiliary contrastive objective alongside next-item prediction. Inference uses the original history capped at the last T items. Training-only recent-suffix cropping with the same next-item target therefore differs in crop anchoring and objective, but sequence cropping itself is established prior art.

Recurrent precedents include [Tan, Xu and Liu (2016)](https://arxiv.org/html/1606.08117v2): GRU training on every prefix paired with its immediate next item, plus stochastic embedding dropout that produces shorter histories. Prefix expansion changes target coverage; suffix cropping can preserve the target while changing context. More directly, [Dang et al. (2026)](https://arxiv.org/html/2604.05309v1) study prefix, suffix and sliding-window splitting, including GRU4Rec. Their suffix construction enumerates contiguous suffixes ending at the same final item. They report substantial interactions between splitting, loss and single/multiple-target supervision, making suffix cropping a close relative of existing training-data construction.

Assessment: novelty would require evidence for the particular stochastic suffix-length policy and its benefit when inference retains the full allowed history. Recommended controls—not established findings—are unchanged full-context training, several fixed recent-context lengths, deterministic cropping matched to the stochastic policy’s mean length, and random-position crops matched by length. Compare uniform versus recency-biased suffix-length distributions and explicitly report the probability of retaining full context. Hold targets, user sampling, loss, negatives and optimization budget constant; evaluate every variant with identical full-history inference. These controls separate stochastic augmentation from simply favoring shorter contexts or reweighting training examples.
